newsitem.title: USA: Applied Materials leads chip equipment stocks rally.
newsitem.headline: Applied Materials leads chip equipment stocks rally.

text.p: Applied Materials Inc. shares surged 13 percent Wednesday, leading a broad charge by semiconductor equipment stocks, a day after the company reported surprisingly strong first-quarter results.
Applied Materials jumped $6.375 to $50.875 on Nasdaq in afternoon trading, leading a rally that pushed the Philadelphia Semiconductor index to a 3.3 percent rise.

Other strong shares in the sector included Novellus Systems Inc., up 6-3/4 to 80-3/4; Lam Research Corp., up 2-7/8 to 40; Lattice Semiconductor Corp., up 4 to 51-1/8; and Teradyne Inc., up 2 to 30-1/8.

On Tuesday, Applied Materials reported profits of $29.6 million, or 16 cents a share, for the quarter ended Jan. 26, after taking a one-time pre-tax charge of $59.5 million, or 32 cents a share after tax, to acquire Opal Inc. and Orbot Instruments Ltd. A year ago, Applied Materials had earnings of $171.6 million.
Revenues fell to $835.8 million from $1.04 billion.
Although the results were down sharply from a year ago, they beat Wall Street estimates and suggested the Santa Clara, Calif.-based company had passed a cyclical bottom.
Several industry analysts raised ratings and price targets for Applied Materials, citing its first quarter pre-charge earnings of 48 cents per share.

Lehman Brothers analyst Edward White repeated his recommendation to buy the stock, and predicted that the price will reach $70 within a year, instead of $62 forecast earlier. White also raised his earnings estimates for the company.
UBS Securities analyst Mark FitzGerald upgraded Applied Materials to buy from hold and also raised earnings estimates for 1997 and 1998.

The sharp rally in Applied Materials' stock sparked a rebound in other shares in its industry. Over the past two weeks, the group had given up considerable ground during a broad sell-off of technology stocks.

"The fact that (Applied Materials) is healthy is definitely contributing to the bounce," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "They are the leader in the semiconductor manufacturing sector."

"The techs were correcting in a normal fashion and now, with the exception of the networkers, seem to have stabilised," he said. "But it doesn't necessarily mean the whole group is going to turn around and storm to the upside."
